prompt: Human: How do I get rid of algae in a pond?
response:
There are several ways to get rid of algae in a pond, but they depend on the type of algae that is causing the problem. Algae that grows on the surface of the water are usually caused by pollutants such as fertilizer or pesticide, or by excess sunlight. Algae that live in the mud or sand are usually caused by too little oxygen in the water, especially if the water is cold and the algae cannot grow as well. 

Approach 1:  Remove Pesticides and Fertilizers

If your pond has been receiving too much fertilizer or pesticide, take the following steps:

Check the package of the pesticide and follow the packaging instructions for disposal. Many pesticides do decompose in water. If the packaging says to throw it away after two years, follow that guideline, even if it is summer. 

If there is an issue with the packaging, remove all the packaging from the pond. This will prevent the pesticide from leaking into the water. 

Contact your local government poison control center and report that you are putting the pesticide in the water. You can learn more about how to report incidents of pesticide use on the EPA website. 

If you live in a region with a lot of pesticides, you may be able to use a compost bin to separate out the pesticides from your garden soil. Compost is considered a safe form of disposal of pesticides and fertilizer. 

Approach 2:  Control Sunlight

When sunlight strikes water, some of it is absorbed, some of it is reflected and some of it is converted to heat. When the sun’s rays hit the water directly, the heat and the reflected light cause algal growth to increase. The more direct sunlight there is, the faster the algal growth will occur. If the sunlight is blocked from reaching the water, the algal growth will delay. 

To control sunlight:

Contact your local government waste disposal service and ask them to take away all plastic, glass, and metal waste containers from your area. 

Contact a local recycle center and ask them to take away all plastic and glass from your area. 

Contact a local yard sale or flea market and ask them to take away all plastic and glass from your area. 

If all else fails, buy a plastic-free container to collect your food scraps, yard waste, and other items that may contain plastic or glass. This will allow you to throw away the containers, and your contents, in a safe and environmentally-friendly manner.
